chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Mufaddal ibn Ibrahim ibn Qays narrated, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal narrated, saying: Tha'laba ibn Maymun narrated from Mu'mar ibn Yahya, from Dawud al-Dajaji, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali, saying:

Amir al-Mu'minin was asked about the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: 'The sects among them disagreed. So woe to those who disbelieve from the view of a great Day.' He said: 'Expect deliverance from three [signs].' It was said: 'O Amir al-Mu'minin, and what are they?' He said: 'Disagreement among the people of Sham, the black banners from Khurasan, and the terror in the month of Ramadan.' It was said: 'And what is the terror in the month of Ramadan?'
'Have you not heard the saying of Allah in the Qur'an: 'If We please, We should send down upon them a sign from the heaven so that their necks should stoop to it?'
It is a sign that will bring the girl out of her veil, awaken the sleeper, and terrify the awake.
ai.seo_question: What are the three signs of deliverance mentioned in relation to the verse 'The sects among them disagreed'?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (as) interprets the verse from Surah Al-Hijr (15:65) regarding the 'disagreement of parties' as a prophetic indicator of three eschatological signs: internal division in Syria, the emergence of the Khurasani banners, and a divine 'Faz'a' (alarm/awe) in Ramadan. This specific Faz'a is elucidated as a celestial sign that compels universal submission, awakening the sleepers and startling the vigilant, thereby fulfilling the Quranic imagery of necks bowing in humility.
